fieldValues.title: Recursive navigation below the root container
fieldValues.summary: Whether navigation recurses below the root container, and if so by what mechanism, is a normative question the concept tree forces. It was ruled by rfc-decision-0750c62f - below the sections, navigation descends the part-of tree - and this unit implements that ruling in srs-rust.
fieldValues.body: Implemented by PR https://github.com/the-greenman/srs-rust/pull/969 (open, auto-merge armed, blocked only on the mirror sync in srs-rust#968). The unit was classified complex when it was written, before rfc-decision-0750c62f ruled consequence 3; it is complicated and Door 1 now, executing that ruling. NavigationNode gains children, skip-serialised when empty so no consumer breaks, and sectionContainerId rides every node at every depth - one tree with named scopes over it, not two trees. repository_navigation_with_depth bounds the descent, with a depth of 0 reproducing the pre-#573 flat list as an escape hatch, exposed as srs repo navigation --depth N. The children come from tree_service::build_tree rather than a second walker, so sibling precedes ordering, depth bounds and cycle pruning stay in one place. The MCP navigation resource and the WASM binding inherit the descent unchanged. Left out deliberately: the spec repo Parts data, nested containers as named scopes (RFC-034 is unimplemented in srs-rust), and RFC-034 Change C retiring the contains traversal in container_service::member_ids, which touches roughly ten tests and is a sibling unit.
